State & Satyajeet Singh vs State on 11 November, 2024 A person may be driving a vehicle at slow speed but he may not be careful, therefore, such a driving would fall into rash or negligent driving. Whereas, other person driving a vehicle at very fast speed but very diligently and carefully having the vehicle under control and that could'nt be termed as a rash or negligent driving. As such, fast speed alone is not a criteria. CA Nos.114/2019 & 128/2019 Satyajeet Singh Vs. State & Anuradha Bhattacharya & Ors. Vs. State & Anr. Page 9 of21 15 It may or may not be there due to alcohol present in CA Nos.114/2019 & 128/2019 Satyajeet Singh Vs. State & Anuradha Bhattacharya & Ors. Vs. State & Anr. Page 11 of21 the body but it must have Satyajeet Singh vs State on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149154840/ 6 had affected the decision making faculties of the appellant Satyajeet. Evidently, speed has its role in the accident. In such circumstances, the only possibility is that speed was excessively high, the appellant having consumed alcohol was having some or the other impairment on his decision making faculties, he was with his friends after an overnight party and was CA Nos.114/2019 & 128/2019 Satyajeet Singh Vs. State & Anuradha Bhattacharya & Ors. Vs. State & Anr. Page 12 of21 enjoying the thrill getting out of the speed. CA Nos.114/2019 & 128/2019 Satyajeet Singh Vs. State & Anuradha Bhattacharya & Ors. Vs. State & Anr. Page 13 of21 22. 23. So far as the defective investigation is concerned, it is to be seen as to whether it was a deliberate act on the part of the investigating Officer or it was bonafide procedural lapse. The lapses in investigation can be ignored as long as the same are not malafide and it does not affect the material aspects of the case. CA Nos.114/2019 & 128/2019 Satyajeet Singh Vs. State & Anuradha Bhattacharya & Ors. Vs. State & Anr. Page 14 of21 24 Similarly, if there are glaring loopholes in the investigation, the defence can exploit the lacunae. The court is to ensure that an innocent person is not put behind bar on trumped-up charges". 25. In this context reference can be made to the judgment in case titled as C. Maniappan v. State of Tamil Nadu [(2010 IX AD (SC) 317] and Ganga Singh v. State of M.P. [(2013 IX AD (SC) 91]. It is, thus, evident that bonafide lapse of the Investigating Officer is not going to help the accused persons. Independent analysis is what is required. If it's found that some lapses are there, but they do not go to the root of the matter and no malafide is there, then such lapses can be ignored. Further, reference can be made to the judgments in Paramjit Singh Vs. State of Punjab [(2007) 13 SCC 530]; Gajoo Vs. State of U.K. [2012) 9 SCC 532; Dayal Singh Vs.
